transcript:
Agent: Thank you for calling card services. My name is Mark. May I have your name, please?
Customer: Hi Mark, my name is Priya Castellan.
Agent: Hello Ms. Castellan. Before we begin, could you please verify your billing zip code and the last four digits of your card?
Customer: Sure, the zip code is 98012 and the last four digits are 4419.
Agent: Thank you. I have your account pulled up. How can I help you today?
Customer: I'm looking at my account, and there is a charge from Ridgeline Cycle Supply that I need help with.
Agent: I see a transaction from Ridgeline Cycle Supply on September 15th. Can you share the details of what happened?
Customer: Yes, it's for $612.40. I had ordered a bicycle from them.
Agent: Okay, and what happened after you placed the order?
Customer: When the delivery truck pulled up to drop it off, we saw right away that the frame was cracked.
Agent: I understand. What took place with the delivery person when you saw the damage?
Customer: I refused the delivery on the spot.
Agent: Did the driver leave the package with you, or did they take it?
Customer: The driver loaded it right back onto the truck and took it with him. I never kept it.
Agent: Have you had any communication with Ridgeline Cycle Supply since the delivery was turned away?
Customer: I sent them an email explaining that the driver took the damaged bike back, but the charge is still sitting on my account.
Agent: Just to make sure I have all the facts down, you purchased a bicycle from Ridgeline Cycle Supply on September 15th for $612.40, but when it arrived with a cracked frame, you refused delivery and the driver took it back, and the merchant has not returned the funds.
